title: Persistent Airflow Review
summary: Integrate exposure, structural and physiological evidence while comparing several plausible respiratory and cardiac hypotheses. Training simulation—not clinical guidance.

mission.role: You are the trainee reviewing progressive respiratory symptoms.
mission.objective: Weigh exposure, structure and physiology to identify the most coherent explanation.

patient.label: Case B — synthetic patient
patient.presentingComplaint: Progressive exertional breathlessness and chronic productive cough.
history: There is a forty pack-year smoking exposure; smoking stopped three years ago.
Symptoms have progressed over several years with limited day-to-day variability.
Sputum volume is modest, with no recorded recurrent pneumonias, orthopnoea or ankle swelling.

findings.label: Upper-airway wall change
findings.description: Illustrative wall thickening follows an upper-lobe airway branch.
findings.significance: This adds spatial context for an airway process but is not independently diagnostic.

findings.label: Illustrative upper-zone region
findings.description: A translucent upper-zone region marks the illustrative structural focus.
findings.significance: This links the structural clue to the lobe-and-segment localisation.

differential.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
differential.description: Persistent airflow obstruction associated with exposure and structural lung change.

differential.label: Asthma
differential.description: Variable airway disease that can coexist with or resemble persistent obstruction.

differential.label: Bronchiectasis
differential.description: Chronic airway dilatation often associated with larger sputum burden or recurrent infection.

differential.label: Heart failure
differential.description: Cardiac dysfunction that can produce exertional breathlessness and respiratory findings.

content.alt: Illustrative histology showing enlarged distal air spaces and reduced alveolar walls.
content.caption: Consider what this structural pattern supports and what it cannot establish alone.

content.heading: Progressive symptoms
content.body: Long tobacco exposure, chronic modest sputum and gradually progressive dyspnoea are recorded, with limited variability and no recurrent pneumonia history.

content.alt: Illustration of bronchioles, alveolar ducts and alveoli.
content.caption: Use the distal-airway and gas-exchange landmarks for localisation.

content.title: Respiratory sound sample
content.transcript: A musical expiratory sound is audible; this finding can occur in more than one airway disorder.

stages.title: Orient
stages.purpose: Connect the opening structural clue to a precise anatomical location.
stages.intro: Use the opening structural clue, then inspect and localise the illustrated upper-zone change.

update.narrative: A progressive low-variability symptom history and long inhalational exposure are recorded.

content.prompt: Determine where the structural change is concentrated and whether the nearby airway-wall change supports the same pattern.
Commit to the lobe, procedural segment and distal structure that best localise the focus.
content.explanation: The illustrated upper-zone focus is paired with an alveolar structural reference.

feedback.hint: Separate the selected region from the tissue structure represented by the opening image.

stages.title: Observe
stages.purpose: Identify which history and physiology findings carry the greatest diagnostic weight.
stages.intro: Identify the strongest evidence while retaining plausible competing hypotheses.

update.narrative: Spirometry and the expiratory sound are available for comparison with the history.

content.prompt: Which observations most strongly support persistent obstructive disease?

options.label: Only brief, fully resolving trigger-linked episodes

content.explanation: Exposure and persistent post-bronchodilator obstruction carry more weight than a non-specific sound.

content.prompt: Classify each finding by its primary evidence domain.

items.label: Enlarged distal air spaces with reduced walls

content.explanation: The image and spirometry contribute independent structural and functional evidence.

content.prompt: Rate each working hypothesis after reviewing the presentation.

stages.title: Interpret
stages.purpose: Test the leading alternatives against the combined evidence without absolute exclusions.
stages.intro: Compare the leading alternatives without treating absent features as absolute exclusions.

update.narrative: Structural, functional and cardiac-context observations are now available together.

content.prompt: Which statement best handles the competing hypotheses?

options.label: COPD is best supported, while asthma, bronchiectasis and heart failure remain less coherent alternatives
Exertional breathlessness alone proves heart failure

content.explanation: The alternatives remain plausible in isolation, but the combined exposure, persistent physiology and structural pattern supports COPD most strongly.

content.prompt: Revise each hypothesis after comparing structural and functional evidence.

stages.title: Conclude
stages.purpose: Commit to the explanation that is coherent across exposure, physiology and structure.
stages.intro: Choose the hypothesis that best explains the full evidence set.

update.narrative: The full patient record is ready for a final evidence-weighted conclusion.

content.prompt: Which reviewed evidence best supports your conclusion?
content.explanation: Exposure, persistent physiology and structural change carry the conclusion together.

feedback.hint: Cite only evidence you reviewed or inspected.

content.prompt: Which diagnosis is best supported by the complete synthetic pattern?

options.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysematous change

content.explanation: Long exposure, persistent post-bronchodilator obstruction and emphysematous structural change converge most strongly on COPD.

expertBenchmark.name: Authored respiratory-educator benchmark

rationales.intermediate-explore: The opening structural clue is carried into an unscored inspection of the illustrated upper-zone findings.
rationales.intermediate-localise: The model lobe and procedural apical segment establish location before the alveolar-unit choice.
rationales.intermediate-key-observations: Exposure and persistent obstruction are stronger than non-specific wheeze.
rationales.intermediate-sort-evidence: Structural and functional evidence should be distinguished before their convergence is assessed.
rationales.intermediate-differential-observe: The initial ratings retain alternatives while prioritising the persistent obstructive pattern.
rationales.intermediate-differential: Each alternative explains part of the presentation, but none explains the full evidence set as coherently.
rationales.intermediate-differential-interpret: The revised ratings reflect the convergence of exposure, physiology and structural evidence.
rationales.intermediate-cite-evidence: The cited history, physiology and structural evidence jointly support the conclusion.
rationales.intermediate-best-diagnosis: The exposure, persistent airflow obstruction and structural change most strongly support COPD.

path.label: Start with structural evidence
path.detail: Inspect the opening image, then connect it to the illustrated upper-zone region.

path.label: Separate structure from function
path.detail: Keep distal air-space change distinct from persistent spirometric obstruction.

path.label: Weight competing hypotheses
path.detail: Test asthma, bronchiectasis and heart failure against the exposure, time course and missing contextual features.

path.label: Synthesize the most coherent diagnosis
path.detail: Choose the hypothesis supported across history, physiology and structure.

evidenceWeights.note: Exposure and progressive low-variability symptoms establish the dominant context.
Persistent post-bronchodilator obstruction is the strongest functional evidence.
The structural pattern supports, but does not independently prove, the leading hypothesis.
The illustrated region provides spatial context and is not patient-derived imaging.
Absent orthopnoea and oedema reduce coherence for heart failure without excluding it.

expertBenchmark.diagnosisRationale: The authored synthesis gives greatest weight to long inhalational exposure, progressive low-variability symptoms and persistent post-bronchodilator obstruction, with emphysematous structural change as support. Asthma, bronchiectasis and heart failure remain plausible partial explanations but fit the full set less well.

debrief.summary: The leading conclusion uses convergent exposure, physiology and structure while retaining asthma, bronchiectasis and heart failure as less coherent alternatives.

keyEvidence.why: The exposure and progressive low-variability course support persistent disease and help compare alternatives.
Persistent obstruction after bronchodilator is the decisive functional evidence.
The opening structural clue supports the leading diagnosis and frames the anatomy tasks.
The illustrative upper-zone region connects observation to lobe-and-segment localisation.
The contextual negatives make heart failure less coherent here but do not act as an absolute exclusion.
